headline: High-risk write-capable coding agent can act on planner output; prompt-injection and data-leakage are limited by LlamaFactory’s non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory is non-runnable with no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Plandex output by default. Plandex can read/write project files and uses review-then-apply, so only a manual or file-based bridge exists. That makes injection possible but not default and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator copies Plandex-generated text into a LlamaFactory prompt or training file, injection becomes possible.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external file-reading harness, file-based prompt injection can occur.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for reviewed, human-authored text.
Strip instructions from any file passed between agents.
Use a one-way export format with no executable markup.
Review Plandex outputs before reuse in any LlamaFactory workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LlamaFactory touches no data classes and has no file or network surfaces, while Plandex reads project files and sends context to a model provider or Plandex Cloud. If sensitive source code is placed in the shared project directory, Plandex can transmit it off-box. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through Plandex, even though LlamaFactory itself is inert.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Plandex’s project directory, Plandex may transmit them to a model provider or cloud backend.
IF LlamaFactory is used as a source of text that is then copied into Plandex, that text can also leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the Plandex workspace.
Use a local/self-hosted model backend for Plandex.
Redact secrets before any file enters the shared project directory.
Run LlamaFactory only on non-sensitive content.
Audit outbound requests from Plandex before enabling auto-apply.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or git capabilities, so it cannot conflict on mutable resources. Plandex can write files, execute shell, and modify git state, and it supports multiple instances via shared backend state. The conflict is therefore one-sided but real when multiple Plandex sessions touch the same repo; uncertainty is low because LlamaFactory is inert.
conditions: IF two Plandex instances operate on the same repository concurrently, file or git conflicts can occur.
IF an external wrapper gives LlamaFactory write access, conflict risk increases beyond this assessment.
mitigations: Run only one Plandex session per repository.
Use git branches or separate worktrees.
Disable auto-apply until changes are reviewed.
Lock the repo during active edits.
Keep LlamaFactory read-only if it is integrated at all.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot act, but Plandex is a coding tool that can execute shell and modify git state. If Plandex consumes LlamaFactory-generated text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or commands. The pathway is plausible through copied outputs, though not automatic because LlamaFactory lacks direct output channels.
conditions: IF Plandex is given LlamaFactory output as task instructions without review, it may act on incorrect facts.
IF auto-apply is enabled, erroneous downstream edits can be committed faster.
mitigations: Require human review of any LlamaFactory-derived text before Plandex uses it.
Keep Plandex in review-then-apply mode.
Ask Plandex to cite file evidence before acting.
Use small, isolated tasks with explicit acceptance criteria.
Disable auto-apply for high-impact repositories.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. LlamaFactory is open-source and non-runnable, while Plandex is open-source but may send context to Plandex Cloud or a model provider. Without a documented data-class mismatch, the compliance risk is limited to operator choice rather than an inherent pair violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Plandex Cloud or a third-party model provider, compliance obligations may change.
IF the operator requires on-prem-only processing, Plandex must be configured accordingly.
mitigations: Use self-hosted Plandex backends for regulated data.
Do not place regulated data in the shared project directory.
Review retention settings before first use.
Document the data flow for any compliance-bound workload.
